chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Devote your affairs to Allah and do not devote them to the people, for whatever is for Allah is indeed for Allah, and whatever is for the people will not ascend to Allah. And do not dispute with the people over your religion, for indeed disputation is a cause of sickness for the heart.

Indeed Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family): [28:56] 'Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.' And He said: [10:99] 'Will you then compel the people until they become believers?'
Leave the people, for the people take from the people, and you all take from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family).

I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He decrees upon a servant that he should enter into this matter (of wilayah), he would be quicker to it than a bird is to its nest.

key_terms.الأمر: Affairs/acts of worship — the totality of one's religious deeds and intentions
key_terms.المخاصمة: Disputation/polemical argumentation — contentious religious debate meant to defeat opponents rather than seek truth
key_terms.ممرضة للقلب: A cause of sickness for the heart — a spiritual pathology that corrupts sincerity
key_terms.هذا الأمر: This matter — a euphemism for wilayah, the guardianship and loyalty to the Imams
key_terms.وكر: Nest — the bird's natural home, used as a simile for the speed and naturalness of divinely decreed guidance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about sincerity for God versus seeking approval from people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses his followers directly with three interconnected exhortations: to dedicate their acts purely to God rather than seeking human approval; to refrain from disputing with opponents over religion, since such disputation corrupts the heart; and to leave guidance to God's will rather than attempting to force it. He reinforces the second point by quoting two Quranic verses (28:56 and 10:99) which were revealed to console the Prophet about his inability to guide his beloved uncle Abu Talib and to forbid compelling others to faith. The hadith concludes with a sublime metaphor transmitted from Imam al-Baqir: that when Allah decrees a person's entry into the wilayah (the path of the Imams), that person rushes toward it with even greater speed than a bird flying to its own nest — emphasizing that true guidance is a divine gift, not a result of human coercion or argumentation.
